title: SEC Filings: Pipeline
description: Filings flowing from discovery to alerts: throughput, Kafka lag and dead letters, LLM summaries, SEC rate limiting, alert delivery, and traces. Metrics are defined in libs/common/src/filings_common/metrics.py; see docs/adr/0016-observability.md.

panels.title: Discovered
panels.description: New filings recorded by discovery in the selected time range. Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: Parsed
panels.description: Filings parsed for the first time in the selected time range (replays and redeliveries don't count again).

panels.title: Summarized
panels.description: Filings summarized and ready for alerts for the first time in the selected time range.

panels.title: Alerts sent
panels.description: Alerts delivered in the selected time range, all channels.

panels.title: Dead letters held
panels.description: Messages in the dead-letter topics now, as measured by their source topics' consumers. Anything above zero needs a look (alert: DLQ not empty).

panels.title: SEC 429s
panels.description: Too Many Requests answers from SEC in the selected time range. Any means the shared rate limit is set too high. Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: Filings per hour, by stage
panels.description: Rolling one-hour totals at each stage. The lines should move together, minutes apart; one that falls behind shows where filings are stuck (the 8-K summaries are the slow step). Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: Discovered per hour, by form type
panels.description: Rolling one-hour totals of new filings, by form type. Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: Consumer lag, by group
panels.description: Messages each consumer group hasn't processed yet, summed over the topic's partitions. Measured by the consumers every 30 seconds (between messages, so it pauses during a long LLM call). The dashed line is the alert threshold (lag high: over 100 for 15 minutes).

targets.expr: sum by (messaging_consumer_group_name, messaging_destination_name) (max by (messaging_consumer_group_name, messaging_destination_name, messaging_destination_partition_id) (filings_consumer_lag))

panels.title: Consumer lag, by partition
panels.description: The same lag per partition (three per topic). One partition far behind the others points at a message that keeps failing there.

panels.title: Events published per hour, by topic
panels.description: Rolling one-hour totals of outbox events the relay published to each topic.

panels.title: Dead letters held, by topic
panels.description: Messages kept in each dead-letter topic. Nothing consumes them: they stay until the topic's retention removes them or an operator trims the topic after fixing and replaying.

panels.title: Dead letters per hour
panels.description: Rolling one-hour count of messages sent to a dead-letter topic, after their retries ran out or a permanent error.

panels.title: LLM call duration, successful calls
panels.description: Rolling one-hour p50 and p95 of each provider's successful calls, validation included. 8-K summaries are minutes apart, so a shorter window would be mostly empty. The local model on CPU takes one to three minutes; Gemini takes seconds.

panels.title: LLM calls per hour, by provider and outcome
panels.description: Rolling one-hour count of calls to each provider: ok, invalid (an answer that failed validation), error, or rate_limited. Calls skipped because a circuit breaker is open aren't calls.

panels.title: Failovers
panels.description: Summaries that came from a fallback provider in the selected time range, because the providers before it failed or were skipped.

panels.title: Circuit breaker opens
panels.description: Times a provider's circuit breaker opened in the selected time range (three failures in a row, or a 429): it is skipped for a minute or more.

panels.title: Failovers and circuit breaker opens per hour
panels.description: Rolling one-hour counts. Failovers are labelled with the provider that answered instead; breaker opens with the provider that is being skipped.

panels.title: Rate-limiter wait per request
panels.description: How long each SEC request attempt waited for the shared token bucket (5 requests a second by default), over the discovery runs of the last hour. Short waits are the limiter working; long ones mean several workers compete for SEC's budget. Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: SEC responses per hour, by status class
panels.description: Rolling one-hour count of SEC responses, retries included: 2xx, 4xx (404 is normal for a company without filings), 5xx, and error (no response). 429s also appear on their own. Discovery is a short-lived job: each run reports its own total in its own series, so runs are added up with max_over_time (increase() needs two values per series; a run usually exports one).

panels.title: Alerts per hour, by channel and outcome
panels.description: Rolling one-hour count of delivery attempts: sent, retry (a transient failure, tried again with backoff), or failed (for good, e.g. a deleted webhook).

panels.title: Delivery success rate
panels.description: Sent alerts as a share of settled ones (sent or failed for good) in the selected time range. Retries aren't settled yet. Permanent failures are usually a user's deleted webhook.

panels.title: Retries
panels.description: Transient delivery failures in the selected time range, each retried with backoff.

panels.title: Recent filing traces
panels.description: One trace per filing, from discovery through the relay, parser, summarizer, and notifier to its alerts. Open a trace ID to see where the filing spent its time.
